nab384588c35.s: Which dynasty ruled the Andhra region immediately after the Ikshvakus, before the Salankayanas?
nab384588c35.x: The order after the Ikshvakus was Brihatpalayanas, Salankayanas, Vishnukundins and then the Eastern Chalukyas.

na9925b9b162.s: Who was the last ruler of the Vishnukundin dynasty?
na9925b9b162.x: Manchana Bhattaraka was the last Vishnukundin ruler; Vikramendra Varma II issued the Chikkulla and Tundi plates and Indrabhattaraka is linked with Ghatikas.

n13bb487ec76.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Undavalli caves?
o: They are situated in Guntur district.
They are situated on the bank of the Godavari.
Their architecture is a Vishnukundina adaptation of the Gupta rock-cut style.
They contain a five-metre reclining image of Ananta Padmanabha Vishnu.
n13bb487ec76.x: The Undavalli caves are on the Krishna in Guntur district, not on the Godavari; the other three statements are correct.

n8efb7655d59.s: The Mogalrajapuram cave complex consists of how many caves?
n8efb7655d59.x: Mogalrajapuram has five caves in all; the fifth is the largest and contains the Shiva Tandava Nataraja sculpture.

nb4d7ba66987.s: How many rock-cut caves are there at Bhairavakonda?
nb4d7ba66987.x: Bhairavakonda, a Kapalika Shaiva centre, has eight rock-cut caves; 4, 9 and 12 are the usual traps.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Salankayanas?
o: They were conquered by Madhava Varma II.
new.x: Vijayapuri was the Ikshvaku capital; the Salankayanas ruled from Vengi (Pedavegi), followed Vaishnavism and were conquered by Madhava Varma II.

new.s: The Anandagotrika (Kandara) kings had their capital at:
new.x: The Chejerla inscription places the Anandagotrika capital at Kandarapuram; Vengi was Salankayana and Vijayapuri Ikshvaku.

new.s: Which historian held that the Vishnukundins were Agnikula Kshatriyas?
new.x: K. Gopalachari called them Agnikula Kshatriyas; B.V. Krishna Rao held they were Brahmins.

new.s: Keesaragutta may mark the beginning of the Vishnukundins as feudatories of the:
new.x: Keesaragutta may mark their start as Vakataka feudatories; the founder Indravarma was a Vakataka vassal.

new.s: Amarapura, the first Vishnukundin capital, is identified with:
new.x: Amarapura is identified with Munnanuru in Amrabad, where yaga-vedikas were found; Tummalagudem was Indrapalanagara.

new.s: Madhava Varma II moved his capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru because of constant wars with the:
new.x: Constant Pallava wars made Madhava Varma II shift the capital to Denduluru and fortify Amarapuri.

new.s: Vikramendra Varma I was the son of Madhava Varma II by a princess of which dynasty?
new.x: Vikramendra Varma I was the son of Madhava Varma II by the Vakataka princess.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Govinda Varma I:
1. He expanded into the Krishna-Godavari region.
2. He bore the title Shadabhigna.
3. He was the founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Govinda Varma I expanded into the Krishna-Godavari region and was called Shadabhigna; the founder was Indravarma.

new.s: How many Rajasuya sacrifices did Madhava Varma II perform?
new.x: Madhava Varma II performed 16 Rajasuyas, 11 Ashvamedhas and 1 Purushamedha.

new.s: From which dynasty did Madhava Varma II take Karma-rashtra up to the Gundlakamma?
new.x: He took Karma-rashtra up to the Gundlakamma from the Pallavas; Vengi was taken from the Salankayanas.

new.s: In the title Trikuta-Malayadhipati of Madhava Varma II, Trikuta refers to:
new.x: Trikuta is Kotappakonda in Guntur; the title came after he defeated the Anandagotrikas.

new.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler is given the title Janasraya in the APPSC key?
new.x: The APPSC (G2 2025) key gives Janasraya to Madhava Varma II, though it is sometimes also given to Vikramendra I.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Shadabhigna was Govinda Varma's title; Mahakavi was Vikramendra I, Satyasraya Indrabhattaraka and Trikuta-Malayadhipati Madhava Varma II.

new.s: The Ipur plates, bearing Lakshmi and conch symbols, belong to:
new.x: The two Ipur plates from Tenali belong to Madhava Varma I.

new.s: The Polamuru plates of the Vishnukundins are noted for describing:
o: A marriage with a Vakataka princess
A grant to a Buddhist vihara
new.x: The Polamuru plates (Ramachandrapuram) describe divine ordeals; the Vakataka marriage is in the Khanapur plates.

new.s: Of the 21 known Vishnukundin inscriptions, how many are copper-plate records?
new.x: The 21 inscriptions comprise 16 copper-plate and 5 stone records.

new.s: Who founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi after the fall of the Vishnukundins?
new.x: Kubja Vishnuvardhana, brother of Pulakeshin II, founded the Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.

new.s: Indrabhattaraka Varma was killed in the Kalinga war by Prithvimula of the:
new.x: Prithvimula of the Ranadurjayas, with a Kalinga king, killed Indrabhattaraka Varma.

new.s: The Jaunpur inscription records a marriage between Indrabhattaraka Varma's daughter and a prince of the:
new.x: Maukhari Ishanavarma defeated Indrabhattaraka, and his son married Indrabhattaraka's daughter (Jaunpur inscription).

new.s: Under the Vishnukundins, Vishti referred to:
new.x: Vishti (Telugu vetti) was forced labour, not a tax; Bhaga was the one-sixth tax.

new.s: Which was the biggest fort in the Telugu country under the Vishnukundins?
new.x: Amrabad was the biggest fort in the Telugu country, with walls of about 200 km.

new.s: How many types of Vishnukundin coins have been found?
new.x: Sixteen types of Vishnukundin coins have been found.

new.s: Vishnukundin coins were discovered by:
new.x: Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam found the Vishnukundin coins.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Vishnukundin coinage?
o: Coins were of iron with a thin copper coating.
Sixteen types of coins are known.
Ship-marked coins point to sea trade.
Coins were mainly of gold and silver.
new.x: Vishnukundin coins were copper-coated iron, not gold or silver.

new.s: A Roman gold coin of Constantine was found at:
new.x: A Roman gold coin of Constantine was found at Kudali Sangameswaram near Alampur.

new.s: Sriparvataswami, the family deity of the Vishnukundins, is identified with:
new.x: Sriparvataswami is Srisaila Mallikarjuna; Amareswara is a common trap.

new.s: The Govinda Vihara at Chaitanyapuri (Hyderabad) was built by:
new.x: Govinda Varma I built the Govinda Vihara at Chaitanyapuri, recorded in a Prakrit inscription.

new.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler granted the village Irundhera to the Paramabhattarika Mahadevi Vihara?
new.x: The Tummalagudem-2 plates record Vikramendra Varma II granting Irundhera to the vihara.

new.s: Who attacked Jainism during the Vishnukundin period?
new.x: Kumarilabhatta attacked Jainism as Kapalika Shaivism rose.

new.s: The Ipur plates record grants to:
new.x: The Ipur plates name Agnisarma and Easwarasarma; Indravarma and Agnivarma were donees of the Mutukali grant.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Ghatikas under the Vishnukundins:
1. They were higher colleges of Sanskrit and Vedic learning.
2. Special Ghatikas existed at Amaravati and Vengi.
3. They are first mentioned in the inscriptions of Madhava Varma II.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Ghatikas were Sanskrit-Vedic colleges with special centres at Amaravati and Vengi; their first mention is in Indrabhattaraka Varma's inscriptions.

new.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler bore the title Vidyadvijaguru?
new.x: Vidyadvijaguru and Janasraya were titles of Madhava Varma II.

new.s: Besides Madhava Varma II, the Janasraya Chhandovichiti is credited to which poet writing in his name?
new.x: The work is credited to Madhava Varma II or to the poet Gunaswami in his name.

new.s: The Akkanna-Madanna caves of the Vishnukundins are located at:
new.x: The Shaiva Akkanna-Madanna caves are on Indrakeeladri, Vijayawada, on the Krishna.

new.s: The Bojjannakonda caves near Visakhapatnam are:
new.x: Bojjannakonda in Visakhapatnam is a Buddhist cave site.

new.s: What was the order of religious use of the Undavalli caves?
new.x: Undavalli was first a Jain abode, then used by Buddhist monks, and finally made a Hindu temple.

new.s: How many main caves does the four-storeyed Undavalli complex have?
new.x: Undavalli has four storeys and three main caves.

new.s: The ground floor of the Undavalli caves is crude and unfinished because the caves were carved:
new.x: Undavalli was carved top-down, so the upper levels are finely detailed and the ground floor was left unfinished.

new.s: Caves 1–3 at Mogalrajapuram have sanctums for the:
new.x: Caves 1–3 have sanctums behind a pillared mandapa for the Trimurti (Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Mogalrajapuram caves:
1. Cave 5, the largest, has a Shiva Tandava Nataraja.
2. They are in Vijayawada (NTR district).
3. They are mainly Vaishnava.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Cave 5 is the largest with a Nataraja and the caves are in Vijayawada; they are mainly Shaiva, not Vaishnava.

new.s: The Durga cave at Mogalrajapuram, with Ardhanarishvara on its back wall, is:
new.x: Cave 4 is the Durga cave with Ardhanarishvara on the back wall; Cave 5 has the Nataraja.

new.s: The Bhairavakonda caves closely resemble the early Pallava caves of:
new.x: Bhairavakonda closely resembles early Pallava caves of Mahabalipuram, hence the attribution debate.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Kapota is the decorated eave above capitals; kumbha is a pot capital, dwarapala a door guardian and the ardhamandapa a pillared hall.

new.s: Vishnukundin brick structural temples with garbhagriha, antarala-mandapa and mukhamandapa are found at:
new.x: Keesaragutta has the brick structural temples; the other three are rock-cut cave sites.

new.s: Vishnukundin cave temples are dated to the:
new.x: Vishnukundin caves belong to the 4th–6th c.; Mahendravarman I's Pallava caves are of the 7th c.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Vishnukundin and Pallava caves?
o: Mahendravarman I's caves belong to the 7th c. CE.
Both follow a mandapa and garbhagriha plan.
Among the Vishnukundin caves, Bhairavakonda is the storeyed one.
Mahendravarman I's caves have lion-based pillars.
new.x: Undavalli, not Bhairavakonda, is the storeyed Vishnukundin cave; the other statements are correct.
